history.reason: I checked the Singletrack thread (Aug 2026) and it is what the card says. Search turns up many Home-Barista threads asking the same thing. Current answers give conflicting tips but no diagnosis order, so a step-by-step fault tree that lets readers keep the machine adds real value.

The diagnosis hinges on Breville's own upper-burr guidance for the BES870 and BES878: the procedure, the range of positions, the factory position, any warning about burr contact, and warranty terms. Every Breville instruction booklet I fetched was a compressed PDF this environment cannot read: BES870 USCM O21 and X26, BES870 ANZ M21, the Williams Sonoma BES870 and BES878 copies, the AJ Madison copy and the archive.org copy. PDF rendering failed because pdftoppm/poppler is not installed. ManualsLib, manualmachine, device.report and notice-facile all returned 403. A human needs to do one of two things. Either supply the extracted text of the 'Adjusting the upper burr / conical burrs' and 'Troubleshooting' pages of the current US booklets (https://assets.breville.com/BES870/BES870_USCM_IB_X26_LR.pdf and https://assets.breville.com/BES878/BES878_USCM_IB_Q26_LR.pdf) with page numbers, or install poppler on the runner so the next research pass can read them. The question to Breville US support about whether adjusting or replacing the upper burr affects the warranty also needs a human. So far the only supported claims are the Barista Pro dial range and starting setting, one owner report, and a parts-seller listing for the upper burr.

With poppler installed, I read the current US Breville booklets for the BES870 (X26) and BES878 (Q26) page by page. Breville supports every step of the diagnosis order: bean freshness, single-wall vs dual-wall basket, dose and tamp, finer dial setting, cleaning the burrs, then the upper-burr adjustment (one step at a time), along with the fast-shot troubleshooting rows. Breville presents the upper-burr adjustment as a feature of the machine, so the 'fix it first' path rests on manufacturer evidence. Three things are still open: the upper-burr number range and factory position, any burr-contact warning, and whether adjustment affects the warranty. The writer can handle them honestly as 'the booklet doesn't say'. They don't block the decision. The stopping rule for buying a grinder is an editorial judgement built on these claims, not a missing fact.

The pages that rank for this question do not give a diagnosis order. Seattle Coffee Gear explains how to remove the top burr but says to go coarser when shots run fast. Complete Home Barista only says to grind finer and has nothing for readers already at setting 1. Forum threads split between shimming, leaving the burr alone and buying a grinder. Breville's own US booklets for the BES870 and BES878 support every free step: roast date, single-wall basket, dose by the tamper cap, burr cleaning, and the upper-burr adjustment, which Breville calls a feature. That gives the post an ordered troubleshooter built on manufacturer evidence, ending with a clear point at which to stop. The open points (burr number range, factory position, burr-contact warning, warranty) are handled openly as things the booklet doesn't say. They do not block the advice.

The brief can be written honestly from the supported claims. Breville's US booklets for the BES870 and BES878 back every free step and the upper-burr procedure. The parts listings and the owner report are labelled as what they are. Four things are stated once as not covered by the booklets: the burr number range, the factory position, a burr-contact warning and the warranty effect. Leave-out items are excluded: the '6' default, shims, grinder recommendations, prices and burr-wear claims.

The draft gives the reader an ordered diagnosis based on Breville's booklets, a test they can run tonight, the correct burr direction and a clear point to stop. The top results for the query are three Home-Barista threads, and none of them offers an order of checks. They mix tips, shims and "buy a grinder" advice. The draft commits to one view: don't buy a grinder yet. It has a keep-yours default and a "When I'd choose differently" section, and it states once what the booklets don't cover. I found only small issues: two unsupported generalisations, a wrong season, and a reference to a troubleshooter tool that doesn't exist in content/tools yet. None of them blocks the post.

Keep the article and its diagnosis order. Change the ending: if after every check the shot is still too fast at setting 1, the built-in grinder is the limit. Don't buy a new machine; buy a separate grinder, and link to our grinder guide for Barista Express/Pro owners with {{guide:...}} (it doesn't exist yet). Write it once for every country: name the machines with {{product:barista-express}} / {{product:barista-pro}}, not Breville or Sage, and drop US-only wording. Don't offer the Barista Express or Pro for sale: leave offerIds empty until a grinder is researched.

I revised the draft to follow the owner's notes and kept the article and its order of checks. The ending now says that if every check is done and the manufacturer can't fix it, the built-in grinder is the limit. The advice is to buy a separate grinder, not a new machine. That points to {{guide:grinder-for-barista-express-and-pro|…}}, a slug I chose because the guide doesn't exist yet. Machines are named with {{product:}} tokens. "Breville" and "US booklet" are gone from the advice; I say "the manual" or "the manufacturer" instead. The methods section says once which booklet editions were read and that other markets' editions weren't compared. offerIds is empty because no grinder has been researched yet. I also applied the judge's optional fixes. I cut the two generalisations no claim supports ('most people who ask…' and 'supermarket beans… most common culprit'). 'This autumn' is now 'in August 2026'. I removed the sentence pointing to an on-page troubleshooter, because content/tools has no grind-fault-tree yet. The tools field still lists the brief's two assets, so whoever publishes this should build those tools or drop them. I added a rough kg conversion next to the lb tamp figure so it reads in every market.

The revision makes the changes the owner asked for, and nothing it was already good at has slipped. The order of checks is unchanged. The ending now settles the decision: "the built-in grinder is the limit. Don't replace the whole machine... Buy a separate espresso grinder", with a link to the grinder guide. Machines are named with {{product:}} tokens and offerIds is empty, as the owner instructed. The top results for the query are Home-Barista threads and the Seattle Coffee Gear top-burr post. None of them gives an order of checks, explains why the pressurised basket hides the grind problem, gives the correct burr direction, or says when to stop. The claims I spot-checked (tamp figure and cap-level dose, the Pro's flow timing, the Allen key being for the shower-screen seal) match the knowledge cards. Before publishing, two links need to resolve: the grinder guide slug and the two listed tools don't exist yet.
the only thing that missing is the offers / link to articles to buy a separate grinder as I think most of the users won't buy a new machine
